findings.title: Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazy
findings.body: Every entry is `import("./x")` placed directly in an object literal. Each call runs the moment `appStore` is first imported, so all ~29 app packages start loading together. This brings none of the lazy-loading benefit that async imports are supposed to provide. Cold start cost and memory stay the same. A failure in any one app module also becomes an unhandled promise rejection at import time. Entries should be thunks (`() => import(...)`) that are called only when an app is needed.

findings.title: async forEach callback escapes the try/catch and is not awaited
findings.body: `forEach(async ...)` returns promises that nothing awaits. The `try/catch` around it cannot catch rejections from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`. Those rejections become unhandled promise rejections. The function also continues to send emails and return `true` before the calendar and video deletions finish. In a serverless context the work can be cut off. This was already a latent problem, but the PR made the callback async without fixing it. Use `await Promise.all(refs.map(...))` inside the try.

findings.title: async forEach callback escapes the try/catch and is not awaited
findings.body: This is the same issue as in the vital copy. The async `forEach` callbacks are fire-and-forget. Errors are not caught by the surrounding try/catch and become unhandled rejections. The handler returns before the calendar and video deletions complete.

findings.title: Un-awaited async forEach in requestReschedule
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` now awaits `getCalendar` inside a callback that nothing waits for. Calendar and video deletions are not completed before the mutation continues or returns. Any rejection is an unhandled promise rejection and is not reported to the caller. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all`.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel deletes are pushed into apiDeletes after it is awaited
findings.body: The recurring branch uses `forEach(async ...)`, which now awaits `getCalendar` before the loop pushes into `apiDeletes`. The pushes therefore happen after the callback yields, which is after `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` has already snapshotted the array. The calendar deletions for recurring bookings are never awaited, and errors become unhandled rejections. The handler may respond before the events are deleted. Before the change `getCalendar` was synchronous, but `deleteEvent` was still awaited inside the callback. The async forEach is still the problem and should become a `for...of` loop or a `Promise.all` over map.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a promise inside `calendar`, and other consumers may not await it
findings.body: `calendar` in the returned objects is now a `Promise<Calendar|null>`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await it. Any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` that uses `item.calendar` synchronously will break. TypeScript may not flag a Promise used with optional chaining. In addition, the promise is created eagerly for every credential, so a rejected promise whose consumer never awaits it becomes an unhandled rejection.

findings.title: await getCalendar added where the enclosing callback may not be async
findings.body: The diff adds `await getCalendar(credential)` inside the reschedule integration cleanup. Only a one-line hunk is shown, so it cannot be verified that the enclosing function is `async`. If this code runs inside a non-async `forEach` or callback, it is a syntax or TypeScript error. If it is `forEach(async ...)`, the pushes into `integrationsToDelete` happen after the array is awaited. Confirm that this is a `for...of` loop in an async scope.
